proposed_capability: Persist the original blocked Play outcome during event-store contention and reconcile the existing private receipt without invoking Play.
operator_correction: Fix both PR #322 review findings before merge approval; preserve the exact-build Windows trial and protected save.
repository_situation: CodeRabbit reproduced the stale launch status on writer timeout and found that the existing race regression can pass without serialization.

competing_theses.thesis: Wait longer for the event lock
competing_theses.evidence: Any finite wait can still expire before the native writer releases the lock.

competing_theses.thesis: Replace the two receipt files with transactional storage
competing_theses.evidence: A format migration is unnecessary for one privately scoped terminal Play receipt and a bounded append-only history.

competing_theses.thesis: Persist a blocked launch receipt with an explicit pending event append
competing_theses.evidence: The existing launch snapshot and per-run event lock can recover the same original observation without re-entering the launcher.

player_save_control_impact: The repair writes only to the selected private receipt run. No game, desktop, save, or installation effect is admitted.
expected_outcome: The original blocked gate remains current during store contention and becomes a single event after receipt-only retry. Native event appends preserve both writers.
negative_tests: Busy receipt reconciliation keeps the saved blocked result
Reconciliation does not launch Play or duplicate history
Removing writer locking makes the contention regression fail
Existing native notices and legacy launch receipts remain readable
rollback_path: Revert the repair commits. Existing receipt schemas and the bounded history are retained. No game or save data is migrated.
unresolved_unknowns: Exact-build Windows adapter and live save, portrait, restock, and responder evidence.
next_gate: Review the offline repairs on PR #322; run the independent Windows named-save trial on the authorized host.
